ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #5
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.

2. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.

3. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.

4. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. Where is the library

5. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. No full stops
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

6. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.

7. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

8. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. run
   C. blue
   D. quickly

9. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

10. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.

11. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only an action
   C. Only a describing word
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

12. When practising Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 14.2.1 Study Skills: Summarising and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject- Verb Agreement and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 14.4.1 Features of style and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Descriptive writing 15.5.1 Functional Writing –Notices and Posters and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.

2. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.

3. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.

4. C — Where is the library?

5. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

6. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.

7. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

8. B — run

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

10. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.

11. D — A person, place, thing, or idea

12. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 14.2.1 Study Skills: Summarising; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject- Verb Agreement; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 14.4.1 Features of style; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Descriptive writing 15.5.1 Functional Writing –Notices and Posters; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
